members.doc:
Stops every thread of Pid, captures registers, stacks, modules and the
memory map, writes Path, and lets the threads go. The crashed thread
takes the registers from the request (the signal frame), since a
tracer would otherwise see the handler's own registers.

members.doc:
Rewrites the raw frames of a report in place. Returns the number of
frames that gained a symbol, 0 when none did (or the host has no
symboliser), -1 when the report could not be read or written. A report
without the pending tag is left alone.

types.name: FAppMenuItem
types.doc:
One entry of the OS-global application menu. The editor builds these
from its own menu model; the platform turns them into the native menu
(NSMenu on macOS). Callbacks fire on the main thread while the menu is
open and must stay valid until the next SetAppMenu call.

members.name: Shortcut
members.doc:
Windows-style display accelerator ("Ctrl+S", "Ctrl+Shift+P"); the
macOS implementation maps Ctrl→⌘ and Alt→⌥ when deriving the key
equivalent. Display-only — dispatching the chord stays the host's
job (the editor's command system already routes keyboard input).

members.name: IsEnabled
members.doc: null = always enabled

members.name: IsChecked
members.doc: null = never checked

members.name: Children
members.doc: SubMenu only

types.name: IPlatformAppMenu
types.doc:
The application-global menu bar. Only macOS renders one (the strip at
the top of the screen); on other platforms IsSupported() is false and
the host keeps its in-window menu widgets.

members.name: SetAppMenu
members.doc:
Replace the app-global menus (everything after the standard
application menu). An empty vector clears them. Item state
(enabled/checked) is re-evaluated from the callbacks each time a
menu opens.

types.name: EConsoleColor
types.doc:
Semantic rather than literal: a backend maps these onto whatever its
terminal understands, and a caller never spells an escape sequence.

members.name: WriteDebuggerString
members.doc:
Goes to the attached debugger's output pane. A no-op where the OS has
no such channel, which is everywhere but Windows.

members.name: MirrorsToDebugger
members.doc:
Whether WriteDebuggerString reaches the OS channel at all: only with a
debugger attached, or MOWO_LOG_DBWIN=1 for a DBWin listener. The channel
is a cross-process lock on Windows, so mirroring unconditionally let one
frozen process stall every other engine process's logging.

Auto-reset: each Signal releases exactly one waiter and the event clears
itself as that waiter wakes. A Signal with nobody waiting stays latched
until the next Wait consumes it.

types.name: IPlatformFile
types.doc:
Paths are UTF-8 throughout, matching IPlatformLibrary::Load. Windows widens
them before touching the OS so names outside the ANSI code page still work.

members.name: MapReadOnly
members.doc:
Maps the whole file read-only and returns its base address, or null when
the OS refused the mapping. ReadAt keeps working on the same handle
either way, so a null here is a fallback and not a failure.

members.name: ReadAt
members.signature: virtual bool ReadAt(FPlatformFileHandle handle, uint64_t offset, void* buffer, size_t size) = 0
members.doc:
Positioned read that moves no shared file pointer, so several threads
may read one handle at once on every platform.

members.name: OpenSharedReadStream
members.doc:
Reads a file another process still holds open for writing. Windows has
to ask for that share mode when it opens the stream; POSIX never denies
it, so there the two openers below differ only in mode.

members.name: OpenSharedWriteStream
members.signature: virtual std::FILE* OpenSharedWriteStream(const std::string& path, bool append) = 0
members.doc:
A writer other processes may read while it is open — the live log,
which the crash reporter and a tail tool read mid-session. Windows
denies other writers only; POSIX never denies anything.

members.name: WriteFileAtomic
members.signature: virtual bool WriteFileAtomic(const std::string& path, const void* data, size_t size) = 0
members.doc:
Replaces path with exactly these bytes, durably: a sibling temp file is
written and flushed to stable storage, then swapped over the target with
a write-through rename, then the directory entry is flushed. A rename on
its own is atomic against a crashed process but not against lost power —
the new name can reach the disk before the data it points at, and the
file then reads as zeros. On failure the target is left untouched, since
it is the last good copy.

members.name: FlushToDisk
members.doc:
The two halves of WriteFileAtomic, for writers that stream into their
own temp file: commit an existing file's data to stable storage, then
swap it over the target with the rename itself made durable.

members.name: SwapIntoPlace
members.signature: virtual bool SwapIntoPlace(const std::string& from, const std::string& to) = 0

members.name: CreateDirectoryWatch
members.signature: virtual FPlatformDirWatchHandle CreateDirectoryWatch(const std::string& path, bool recursive) = 0
members.doc:
Blocking directory-change primitive under the hot-reload watchers. Wait
blocks up to timeoutMs and fills absolute paths of changed entries; true
with an empty result is a timeout, false means the watch is dead. Cancel
wakes a Wait blocked on another thread and kills the watch; Close frees
it and must only run once no Wait is in flight.

members.name: WaitForDirectoryChanges
members.signature: virtual bool WaitForDirectoryChanges(FPlatformDirWatchHandle handle, int32_t timeoutMs, std::vector<std::string>& outChangedPaths) = 0

members.name: GetSymbol
members.signature: virtual void* GetSymbol(void* handle, const char* name) = 0

members.name: Prefix
members.doc:
Filename prefix the linker gives a shared library: "lib" on POSIX,
empty on Windows.

members.name: ModuleFileName
members.doc:
The on-disk filename for a module, prefix and extension included —
"MowoEngine.Platform.dll" on Windows, "libMowoEngine.Platform.dylib" on
macOS (FBinaryNames::ModuleStem). Building it as
`name + Extension()` is a Windows-shaped bug: it names a file that does
not exist on POSIX, and every caller doing so was silently failing to
find plugin binaries there.

members.name: OwnsAddress
members.signature: virtual bool OwnsAddress(void* handle, const void* address) = 0
members.doc:
True when `address` falls inside the loaded image `handle` refers to.
Used to attribute a static registration back to the module that owns it.

members.name: AddSearchDirectory
members.doc:
Add a directory to the process's shared-library search path so
subsequent by-name loads (ours AND any a vendor runtime performs
internally) can resolve from it — packaged games use this for
Binaries/<platform>/Upscalers. Default: no-op.

members.name: LoadedImagePath
members.doc:
Full path of an image with this file name already mapped into the
process, or empty. The Windows loader keys a load by FULL path, so a
plugin a host links (the test executables link every plugin) and a plugin loader
then loads from Plugins/<X>/Binaries/ come up as two copies with two sets
of registries. The POSIX loaders already hand back the mapped image for a
matching SONAME / install name, so the default answers empty.

members.name: MappedImageSymbol
members.signature: virtual bool MappedImageSymbol(const std::string& path, const char* name, void*& outSymbol) = 0
members.doc:
Whether the image at `path` (the executable for an empty path) is mapped
into the process, and if it is, the address of the symbol `name` THAT
image exports, or null in `outSymbol` when it exports none. A by-handle
dlsym also searches the image's dependencies, which would hand back a
dependency's copy of a symbol every image defines (the build id).
Takes no reference on the image.

members.name: OpenImageForLoad
members.doc:
A module file held open across a verified load. The signature gate hashes
the bytes through this handle, and on Windows nobody can write, rename or
delete the file until CloseImageForLoad, so the image Load maps is the one
that was verified — checking a path and then loading the path left a window
in which the file could be swapped. POSIX cannot deny writers: there
ImageStillAtPath catches a path renamed over and any write to the held
inode through its change time (ctime, which utimes() cannot set back), so
an in-place rewrite of the same size with a restored mtime is caught too.
Null when the file cannot be opened.

members.name: ReadImage
members.signature: virtual int64_t ReadImage(void* image, uint64_t offset, void* dst, uint64_t size) = 0
members.doc: Bytes read at `offset` (0 at the end of the file, -1 on an error).

members.name: ImageStillAtPath
members.signature: virtual bool ImageStillAtPath(void* image, const std::string& path) = 0
members.doc: False when `path` no longer names the file the handle holds.

members.name: ImportedLibraryNames
members.doc:
The shared libraries the image pulls in when it is mapped: the PE import
and delay-import tables, ELF DT_NEEDED, Mach-O LC_LOAD_DYLIB and its weak,
lazy, upward and re-export forms (a fat image answers for this host's
slice). Empty where the format is not parsed — the dependencies then load
unverified.

members.name: ResolveImportForLoad
members.doc:
The file the loader would map for an import of this name when that is a
file the game ships: empty for an image already mapped, an OS library or
an API set, which the gate has no signature for and no reason to doubt.

members.name: RestrictSearchPath
members.doc:
Takes the working directory and PATH out of the shared-library search, so
a DLL dropped beside a shortcut's target or anywhere on PATH is never
what an import resolves to. The application directory and the
directories AddSearchDirectory named stay searched. False where the
platform has no such switch.

members.name: PlatformName
members.doc:
Platform id used by every binaries layout ("win-x64", "linux-x64",
"osx-arm64", "android-arm64", "ios-arm64") — Engine/Binaries/<id>,
a package's Binaries/<id>, Plugins/<X>/Binaries/<id>.

members.name: GetPreferredLanguages
members.doc:
The user's UI languages, most preferred first, as BCP-47-ish tags
("ru-RU", "en"). Empty when the OS exposes no preference — a
Finder/desktop launch with no LANG in the environment is the common
case, so callers must have a fallback rather than treating an empty
list as an error.

members.name: GetPreferredLanguage
members.doc: The first preferred language, or an empty string.

members.name: TotalPhysicalBytes
members.doc: Installed physical RAM.

members.name: AvailablePhysicalBytes
members.doc:
Physical RAM the OS still has available. Not total minus our working
set - the rest of the machine counts too.

members.name: ProcessWorkingSetBytes
members.doc: This process's resident set: what a task manager shows on our row.

members.name: ProcessPeakWorkingSetBytes
members.doc:
The peak that working set has reached over the process lifetime, which
is the number that decides whether a machine will swap.

members.name: EnableHeapLeakReporting
members.doc:
Turn on whatever heap leak reporting the platform CRT offers, dumping
at exit. Only the MSVC debug CRT implements it today; elsewhere it is a
no-op returning false, because a leak checker that silently does
nothing is worse than one that says it is unavailable.

members.name: AllocateSecretPages
members.doc:
Pages for secrets (archive keys) a crash dump must not carry: committed
read-write straight from the OS, locked so they never reach the page
file, excluded from core dumps where the OS offers it (MADV_DONTDUMP),
and never heap memory — so which module allocates does not matter, and
the minidump writers can name the exact range to leave out. `size` is
rounded up to whole pages; null on failure.

members.name: FreeSecretPages
members.signature: virtual void FreeSecretPages(void* address, size_t size) = 0
members.doc:
Zeroes the block, unlocks it and returns it to the OS. `size` is what
was passed to AllocateSecretPages.

members.name: PageSize
members.doc: The page size AllocateSecretPages rounds to.

members.name: UserAppDataDir
members.doc:
Legacy per-user root (Roaming AppData / $XDG_CONFIG_HOME / Application
Support). Kept only as the migration source for data written by builds
that predate the Local/state split — new code uses the three roots below.

members.name: UserConfigDir
members.doc: Config root: %LOCALAPPDATA% / $XDG_CONFIG_HOME / Application Support.

members.name: UserStateDir
members.doc:
State root (logs, crashes, savegames): %LOCALAPPDATA% / $XDG_STATE_HOME
(~/.local/state) / Application Support.

members.name: UserCacheDir
members.doc:
Cache root (regenerable data): %LOCALAPPDATA% / $XDG_CACHE_HOME
(~/.cache) / ~/Library/Caches.

members.name: SystemFontsDir
members.doc:
Where the OS keeps its own fonts, with a trailing separator. The UI
falls back to a system face when a themed one is missing.

types.name: EProcessLifetimeSupport
types.doc:
How tightly a host can bind a child process's lifetime to ours. The three
answers are genuinely different guarantees, and a caller that cannot tell
them apart ends up promising a user something the OS never agreed to.

members.name: None
members.doc: Nothing at all - a child survives us however we die.

members.name: BestEffortOnShutdown
members.doc:
The parent kills the children it registered on its way out: normal
shutdown, an immediate exit, and the fatal-signal path. An untrappable
kill of the parent (SIGKILL, a power cut) still orphans them.

members.name: KernelEnforced
members.doc: The kernel enforces it - the child dies with us however we die.

members.name: SpawnProcess
members.signature: virtual FProcHandle SpawnProcess(const std::string& executable, const std::vector<std::string>& args, const std::string& workingDir, bool detached) = 0

members.name: SpawnProcessWithEnvironment
members.signature: virtual FProcHandle SpawnProcessWithEnvironment(const std::string& executable, const std::vector<std::string>& args, const std::string& workingDir, const std::vector<std::pair<std::string, std::string>>& environment) = 0
members.doc:
Spawn with `environment` laid over the inherited environment (a name that
already exists is replaced). The games launcher hands a game the port and
session token of its SDK link this way: a command-line argument would show
up in every process list, an environment block does not.

members.name: ProcessIdOf
members.doc: The OS process id behind a handle, 0 for a null or dead handle.

members.name: SpawnProcessWithOutput
members.signature: virtual FProcHandle SpawnProcessWithOutput(const std::string& executable, const std::vector<std::string>& args, const std::string& workingDir, bool hideWindow, FProcPipeHandle& outRead) = 0
members.doc:
Spawn with stdout and stderr merged into one readable pipe. Four call
sites hand-rolled this over CreateProcess + CreatePipe; they all wanted
the same thing, which is a child whose output can be streamed into a log
view without blocking the caller.

`outRead` is only valid when the call succeeds, and the caller owns it:
close it with ClosePipe once ReadPipe reports end of stream.

members.name: SpawnCommandLineWithOutput
members.signature: virtual FProcHandle SpawnCommandLineWithOutput(const std::string& commandLine, const std::string& workingDir, bool hideWindow, FProcPipeHandle& outRead) = 0
members.doc:
Same pipe contract for callers that assemble one raw command line (mbt
through cmd.exe, packaging jobs) rather than an executable plus argument
list. POSIX runs the line through /bin/sh -c.

members.name: ReadPipe
members.signature: virtual int32_t ReadPipe(FProcPipeHandle pipe, void* buffer, int32_t size) = 0
members.doc:
Blocks until there is something to read. Returns bytes read, 0 once the
child has closed its end, and -1 on a real error - a caller loops until
it stops being positive.

members.name: SpawnChildTiedToParent
members.signature: virtual FProcHandle SpawnChildTiedToParent(const std::string& executable, const std::vector<std::string>& args, const std::string& workingDir, bool hideWindow, FProcPipeHandle* outRead) = 0
members.doc:
Spawn a child already bound to our lifetime, as tightly as this host
allows. The tie belongs to the call, not to which spawn overload the
caller happened to reach for: PR_SET_PDEATHSIG can only be armed by the
child between fork and exec, so a plain SpawnProcess can never be given
the kernel tier afterwards however politely it asks.

Pass a non-null `outRead` to also take the merged stdout/stderr pipe,
under SpawnProcessWithOutput's ownership rules.

members.name: GetChildLifetimeCapability
members.doc:
What that tie is actually worth here, plus a name fit for a log line or
a test's per-platform expectation. A bool would answer false both for a
host with no mechanism and for a call that merely failed, and callers
have already read one as the other.

members.name: KillChildWhenParentDies
members.doc:
Tie an already-spawned child's lifetime to ours, so an editor that
crashes or is killed does not strand a build or a PIE client running
headless forever. Reaches the kernel tier only where the mechanism can
be granted retroactively (a Windows job object); elsewhere it registers
the child for the best-effort teardown, which is why a caller that can
choose spawns through SpawnChildTiedToParent instead.

members.name: IsChildTiedToParent
members.doc: Whether this handle is currently registered for parent-death.

members.name: GetTiedChildCount
members.doc:
Registered children still alive. Counting prunes the ones that already
exited, so a long editor session does not accumulate dead entries.

members.name: KillTiedChildren
members.doc:
Kill every registered child now. The shutdown paths call this; a host
that tears itself down some other way calls it directly.

members.name: WaitForProcess
members.signature: virtual bool WaitForProcess(FProcHandle handle, int32_t& outExitCode) = 0

members.name: KillProcessTree
members.doc:
Kill the process and every descendant it spawned. KillProcess alone
leaves grandchildren running — a cancelled build keeps its compilers.

members.name: IsProcessIdRunning
members.doc:
Whether any process with this id is running, whoever started it. For
reclaiming files a dead session left behind: a reused id reads as alive,
which only ever keeps a file longer, never deletes a live one.

members.name: ExecutableFileName
members.doc: "MowoServer" → "MowoServer.exe" on Windows, unchanged elsewhere.

members.name: OpenInShell
members.signature: virtual bool OpenInShell(const std::string& target, const std::string& args, const std::string& workingDir, bool hidden) = 0

members.name: ExitCurrentProcessImmediately
members.doc:
Terminate the current process with `exitCode` WITHOUT running C runtime
atexit handlers or DLL detach. A host that has already torn down through
its own Shutdown() uses this to skip the static-destruction phase, where
unloading cross-DLL static state can fault under the debug CRT.

members.name: InstallShutdownHandler
members.doc:
Route the OS's terminate request (SIGTERM/SIGINT; console Ctrl-C /
close / system shutdown on Windows) to `handler` instead of the
default instant kill. The handler runs on an OS-chosen thread — it
may only set a flag the main loop polls; a headless host uses this
for a graceful stop (notify clients, tear down, exit 0).

members.name: RouteDebugReportsToStderr
members.doc:
Send the C runtime's debug assertion and error reports to stderr instead
of a modal dialog. A headless test row inside a windowed host has nobody
to press the box, so an assert read as a wedge until the runner's
timeout; on stderr the report is printed and the process ends with a
decodable exit. No-op where the runtime has no dialog mode.

members.name: ShowStartupError
members.signature: virtual void ShowStartupError(const std::string& title, const std::string& message) = 0
members.doc:
A failure the process cannot start past, reported before any window or
log exists: always on stderr, and where the process has no stderr to
write to (an editor started from the desktop) also in a message box, or
the process would simply vanish.

members.name: InvalidHandle
members.doc:
The value no live socket ever takes. Compare against this rather than
against -1: Winsock's invalid handle is not -1.

members.name: Startup
members.doc:
Winsock needs this before any other call; POSIX does not and returns
true. Reference-counted, so pairs of Startup/Shutdown nest safely.

members.name: CreateUdpSocket
members.doc:
The PIE free-port probe binds UDP because that is what the session will
bind afterwards — a TCP probe can report a port some UDP listener holds.
BindAndListen with backlog 0 covers the bind; listen never applies.

members.signature: virtual bool SetReuseAddress(FPlatformSocketHandle handle, bool reuse) = 0

members.name: SetNoDelay
members.signature: virtual bool SetNoDelay(FPlatformSocketHandle handle, bool noDelay) = 0

members.name: BindAndListen
members.signature: virtual bool BindAndListen(FPlatformSocketHandle handle, const std::string& address, uint16_t port, int32_t backlog) = 0
members.doc:
An empty address binds to the loopback interface, which is what every
caller here wants - a debug port open to the network is a liability.

members.name: GetBoundPort
members.signature: virtual bool GetBoundPort(FPlatformSocketHandle handle, uint16_t& outPort) = 0
members.doc:
The port the OS actually assigned, which matters after binding to port 0
to ask for any free one.

members.name: Connect
members.signature: virtual bool Connect(FPlatformSocketHandle handle, const std::string& address, uint16_t port) = 0
members.doc:
Client side. An empty address connects to loopback, matching
BindAndListen so a test can pair the two without repeating "127.0.0.1".

members.name: Accept
members.doc:
Returns InvalidHandle() when nothing is waiting on a non-blocking
listener, which is not an error.

members.name: Send
members.signature: virtual int32_t Send(FPlatformSocketHandle handle, const void* data, int32_t size, bool& outWouldBlock) = 0
members.doc:
Bytes moved, 0 for a closed peer, negative for an error. A non-blocking
socket with nothing to read reports 0 bytes and sets outWouldBlock, so a
caller can tell "not yet" from "gone".

members.name: Receive
members.signature: virtual int32_t Receive(FPlatformSocketHandle handle, void* buffer, int32_t size, bool& outWouldBlock) = 0

members.name: SetBroadcast
members.signature: virtual bool SetBroadcast(FPlatformSocketHandle handle, bool broadcast) = 0
members.doc:
Datagrams, for the editor's LAN session beacon: a UDP socket allowed to
broadcast sends to "255.255.255.255", and a receive reports who sent
what arrived (dotted IPv4 and port). Same return and outWouldBlock rules
as Send / Receive.

members.name: SendTo
members.signature: virtual int32_t SendTo(FPlatformSocketHandle handle, const void* data, int32_t size, const std::string& address, uint16_t port, bool& outWouldBlock) = 0

members.name: ReceiveFrom

members.name: LastError
members.doc:
The calling thread's last socket error code (WSAGetLastError / errno),
for diagnostics after a third-party socket layer reports a bare
failure. 0 when the platform keeps no such state.

members.name: MaxThreadNameLength
members.doc:
Longest name the OS records, terminating null included; 0 means the OS
imposes no limit worth honouring. Linux caps pthread_setname_np at 16
and rejects the whole call past that, so a caller that wants the name
to survive has to shorten it into something still recognisable.

members.doc:
False where only the running thread can rename itself: macOS takes no
thread argument on pthread_setname_np, so SetThreadName against another
thread's handle does nothing there.

members.name: SetCurrentThreadPriority
members.doc:
True only when the OS actually applied the priority. Raising a thread
above normal needs CAP_SYS_NICE on Linux and is refused outright rather
than reported as success.

members.name: CurrentThreadId
members.doc:
The calling thread's OS-native id — the number debuggers, crash dumps
and the Vulkan validation layer print, NOT std::thread::id. Used to
correlate external reports with engine thread roles.

members.name: Seconds
members.doc:
Monotonic seconds since an arbitrary origin fixed at process start.
Never walks backwards and is unaffected by wall-clock adjustments.

members.name: Cycles
members.doc:
Raw counter + its frequency, for callers that want to hold a

members.name: BeginHighResolutionSleep
members.doc:
Windows rounds a sleep up to the scheduler tick (~15.6 ms by default),
which makes any frame cap overshoot badly. A frame pacer brackets its
sleeping with these; the calls nest and are no-ops where the OS clock
already has sub-millisecond granularity.

members.signature: virtual void LocalTime(int64_t unixSeconds, std::tm& out) = 0
members.doc:
Reentrant calendar breakdown of a Unix timestamp. Plain std::localtime
shares one static tm; the reentrant spelling differs per C library
(localtime_s takes its arguments the other way round from localtime_r).

members.name: UtcTime

members.name: UtcTimeToUnixSeconds
members.doc:
The inverse of UtcTime: a calendar time read as UTC, back to epoch
seconds. std::mktime would read it as LOCAL time and silently shift the
result by the machine timezone, which is why this is not just mktime.

Commands return false when the platform did nothing, so the caller can

The rectangle spanning every attached display, in the desktop
coordinate space windows are positioned in. It can start negative
when a monitor sits left of or above the primary one, which is why
the origin is reported rather than assumed to be zero. False when
the platform cannot answer - the caller then clamps to positives.

members.name: GetMonitorRects
members.signature: virtual int32_t GetMonitorRects(int32_t maxCount, int32_t* outRects)
members.doc:
Individual monitor rectangles in the same desktop space. The virtual
screen is their bounding UNION, which contains dead space on
non-rectangular arrangements — a window clamped only to the union can
restore fully invisible. Fills up to maxCount rects as x,y,w,h
quadruples and returns how many monitors exist; 0 = unsupported and
the caller falls back to the union clamp.

types.name: FCrashRegisters
types.doc:
General-purpose register file in a CPU-neutral shape; the collector fills
what its platform exposes.
X64:   gpr[0..15] = rax rcx rdx rbx rsp rbp rsi rdi r8..r15 (the
CONTEXT_AMD64 order), pc = rip, sp unused (rsp is gpr[4]).
Arm64: gpr[0..30] = x0..x28, fp, lr; sp and pc separate.

members.name: OpenRational
members.signature: virtual bool OpenRational(const std::string& path, uint32_t width, uint32_t height, uint32_t fpsNumerator, uint32_t fpsDenominator, uint32_t bitrateKbps, uint32_t audioSampleRate, uint32_t audioChannels) = 0
members.doc:
Width and height must be even. Bitrate 0 picks one from the frame size.
The rate is fpsNumerator / fpsDenominator, so NTSC 23.976 is 24000/1001
and the frame clock never drifts from the one an edit expects. Audio
rate and channels of zero mean no audio track; otherwise AAC takes 44100
or 48000 Hz, one or two channels, and anything else is refused rather
than resampled here.

driver that decodes wrong.
